chunks: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Two bloods in Islam are permissible by Allah — none shall execute judgment regarding them until Allah sends our Qa'im of the Ahlulbayt. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends our Qa'im of the Ahlulbayt, he will judge regarding them both with Allah's judgment, requiring no proof against them: the married adulterer — he will stone him; and the withholder of zakat — he will strike his neck.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

key_terms.الزَّانِي الْمُحْصَنُ: the married adulterer (one who commits zina while having a living spouse in a valid marriage)
key_terms.بَيِّنَة: proof/evidence (formal legal testimony required in hudud cases)
key_terms.دَمَانِ حَلَالٌ: two permissible bloods (two cases where capital punishment is lawful)
key_terms.قَائِمَنَا أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: our Qa'im of the Ahlulbayt (the awaited Imam al-Mahdi)
key_terms.مَانِعُ الزَّكَاةِ: the withholder of zakat (one who refuses to pay the obligatory alms-tax)

ai.seo_question: What punishments will the Imam al-Mahdi (Qa'im) carry out without requiring witnesses according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that two capital punishments in Islamic law — stoning the married adulterer and beheading the withholder of zakat — are divinely sanctioned but remain unexecuted until the Qa'im (al-Mahdi) of the Ahlulbayt rises. This hadith reflects the Shia theological position that certain hudud punishments are suspended in the absence of the infallible Imam, who alone has the divine authority to carry them out without requiring witness testimony. The original audience — followers of the Imam during the Abbasid period — would have understood this as a directive to defer application of these specific rulings to the time of al-Mahdi's emergence.
